title: mkDashRamp single-pass dashes below a density threshold, band mechanism kept at the dark end (Jay decision 12=B, SESSION-SUMMARY.md §4 item 12)
decision: Jay decision 12=B, 2026-09-17: "T3b, a new unit -- draw single-pass dashes below some density threshold, keeping the band mechanism where it earns its keep. The cost is a new threshold to justify and another mode boundary in a file that already has several."
acceptance_bar: at the sparse end, mkDashRamp dashes must read as single-pass strokes riding the rulings, not multi-pass bundles/tiles; T3's own count (>=40 @ d=1) and monotonicity (d=1..med) bars must still hold; the band mechanism (T4, Jay decision 1=B) must remain intact at the dark end (d=220 >= 1500mm, no slab, G4 30/30).

mechanism: surface-fill.js: `MK_BAND_MAX_PASSES=6` was a density-BLIND ceiling on mkDashRamp's parallel-pass band (T4's own mechanism, Jay decision 1=B). New `bandOnsetCap(density)` ramps the EFFECTIVE per-mark pass ceiling from 1 (single pass) at d=1 up to the full MK_BAND_MAX_PASSES by MK_BAND_ONSET_D=35 -- measured as the last integer density at which the ungated mechanism already sat at its 6-pass ceiling naturally, on every one of {sphere,torus}x{addLayer,create}. At and above MK_BAND_ONSET_D the gate is a byte-identical no-op. `bandOnsetCap` is read in exactly the two places `MK_BAND_MAX_PASSES` used to be read directly: solveAt's `bandN` (feeds `capOf`, which bounds how much ink ONE mark can carry) and layMark's morph-branch `bandN` recompute (must agree with solveAt's own value) -- both gated to `law.shape === 'morph'`, unique to mkDashRamp.

ramp_internal_step_disclosure.note: STOP-AND-REPORT, not hidden (AGENT-PROTOCOL 'stop-and-report beats a fudge'): WITHIN the gated zone (d<35) the ramp's own individual integer-pass steps are NOT all sub-drift-envelope. O8 (T4's own guard) pins bandMax>=2 exactly at d=50, which forces ANY threshold this unit could choose to sit strictly below 50 -- and per measurement_2 above, the band is genuinely load-bearing (34-76% of total ink) at EVERY density below ~70. A hard on/off switch anywhere below 50 would cost that same 34-76% in ONE cliff; the ramp instead spreads it across several smaller integer-pass steps. The largest single step measured (addLayer & create rigs, sphere, d=4->5, the 1-pass->2-pass transition) is 59-76%, larger than ordinary density-to-density drift (a few percent in the unmodified baseline) -- inherent to any discrete integer-pass mechanism gated below 50, not an artifact of a poor threshold choice.

evidence.what_i_saw: sphere/hatch/mkDashRamp/low (both rigs): BEFORE shows 6 curving rows, several of which fan out into 4-6 clearly-separated parallel hairlines that all start/stop together -- reads as thick ribbon bundles, exactly the 'row-wide tile' STILL-OPEN.md flagged. AFTER: the SAME 6 rows now draw as single, crisp, curving strokes with visible dash gaps -- reads unambiguously as discrete dashes riding the rulings, not bundles. A 3x-native crop of the darkest (upper-left) region makes this unambiguous: BEFORE shows three separate 4-6-line fanned bundles; AFTER shows three separate single hairlines with real gaps between segments. torus/hatch/mkDashRamp/low shows the identical improvement in kind (same crop comparison). sphere/torus max (d=220, both rigs) are pixel-for-pixel byte-identical to the pre-T3b tree -- the dark-end gradient T4 built is untouched.

open_follow_ups: The ramp's own largest internal step (d=4->5, 59-76%) exceeds ordinary density drift -- disclosed and fingerprinted, not hidden, but a future unit could investigate a non-integer/blended pass mechanism if this is judged too abrupt on the app's own live density slider.

torus/addLayer/d=1 mark count moved 37->38 (a gain), a side effect of `L`'s own shorter cap changing the placement-exclusion geometry -- disclosed under Bars changed, does not touch T3's own unpinned torus behavior (T3-impl.md itself calls torus a secondary, non-gated check).
